issues.legal_issue: Capital-gains liability depends on whether title to each asset was transferred after the statutory commencement date.
material_facts: The transaction covered immovable properties and movable properties, with separate values assigned to each group.
The immovable properties were conveyed by a registered sale deed executed after the commencement of the capital-gains provision; the earlier agreement to sell did not transfer title to them.
The movable properties were delivered to the transferee before that commencement, and title to them passed on delivery.
issues.conclusion: Profits attributable to the immovable properties were chargeable, while profits attributable to the movable properties were not chargeable under the provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, capital gains were chargeable only for a sale, exchange or transfer of a capital asset effected after the provision commenced. For the assets in this case, title to immovable property passed on conveyance, while title to movable property passed on delivery.

predicates.capital_gains_tax_proceeding: The dispute concerns the assessment of profits as capital gains.
predicates.immovable_property_conveyed_after_commen: The transferor conveyed the immovable property after the capital-gains charge had commenced.
predicates.movable_property_delivered_before_commen: The transferor delivered the movable property, thereby passing title, before the capital-gains charge had commenced.

issues.definition: When a capital-gains assessment concerns immovable property conveyed after commencement and movable property delivered before commencement, profits from the former are chargeable and profits from the latter are not.

issues.legal_issue: A request for further inquiry cannot be raised for the first time before the High Court when it was not sought from the Tribunal.
material_facts: In a reference from the Tribunal, the appellant argued that the distinction between movable and immovable properties required further evidence and sought a remand.
The appellant had not applied to the Tribunal for an inquiry on that distinction.
The High Court declined to order a remand.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in declining to entertain the request for a remand.
issues.legal_principle: In a reference under section 66(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a party that considers further inquiry necessary must seek it from the Tribunal; having failed to do so, it cannot call on the High Court to remand the matter for that purpose.

predicates.high_court_tax_reference: The matter is before the High Court on a reference from a tax tribunal.
predicates.further_inquiry_not_requested_from_tribu: The party seeking further evidence did not ask the tribunal to order an inquiry.
predicates.remand_request_first_raised_before_high_: The party first asked for a remand before the High Court.

issues.definition: When a party in a High Court tax reference did not request an inquiry from the tribunal and first seeks a remand before the High Court, the High Court may decline to order one.

issues.legal_issue: Fixtures listed among movable assets are not conveyed by a separate deed of immovable property when the transaction documents show that the deed covers only the immovable-property schedule.
material_facts: The agreement and schedule divided the properties into two parts, one for immovables and one for movables, and assigned separate prices to each part.
The sale deed conveyed only the properties in the immovable-property part and stated a price corresponding to that part alone.
The fixtures at issue were listed in the movable-property part, and the transaction documents showed that the parties intended that part, including the fixtures, to pass by delivery.
The deed did not expressly include the fixtures listed in the movable-property part.
issues.conclusion: The sale deed conveyed only the immovable properties in its schedule and did not convey the fixtures listed as movables; the Tribunal’s decision to tax only profits attributable to the properties conveyed by that deed was correct.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that a transfer ordinarily passes the transferor’s interests and legal incidents, including things attached to the earth, unless a different intention is expressed or necessarily implied. The deed must be construed with the underlying agreement; the separate schedules and prices, the deed’s limited description of the conveyed property, and the stated intention that the second-part properties pass by delivery showed that the fixtures were not conveyed by the deed.

predicates.capital_gains_tax_proceeding: The dispute concerns the assessment of profits as capital gains.
predicates.fixtures_listed_with_movable_assets: The transaction documents list the fixtures among the assets treated as movable property.
predicates.separate_prices_for_property_groups: The transaction documents assign separate prices to the immovable-property group and the movable-property group.

issues.definition: When fixtures are listed with movable assets, the property groups have separate prices, the deed is limited to the immovable-property schedule, and the documents show an intention for the movable group to pass by delivery, those fixtures are not conveyed by the deed.
